articles.title: Selinsgrove Borough Council approves townhome/commercial plan
articles.summary: SELINSGROVE — Selinsgrove Borough Council has approved a land development plan for 12 townhouses and up to six commercial spaces on North Market Street.

articles.title: Keystone Completes Office-to-Residential Conversion Project in Philadelphia
articles.summary: PHILADELPHIA — Local developer Keystone has completed an office-to-residential conversion project in Philadelphia’s Independence Mall district. Designed by Tantillo Architecture and built by Fasttrack Construction, the project transformed the historic, 12-story building at 400 Market St. into a 176-unit apartment complex known as 400 Market Flats. articles.title: White Cap opens 480,940-square-foot distribution center in Bethlehem
articles.summary: White Cap opened a 480,940-square-foot Enterprise Distribution Center in Bethlehem to serve 67 branches across 13 states and boost Lehigh Valley jobs.

articles.title: Developer of proposed Pa. data center campus offers to buy opponents’ property
articles.summary: PNK Group is willing to pay fair market price plus a premium in Union County.

articles.title: Rutter’s brings back SPAM menu with expanded lineup for limited time
articles.summary: Rutter’s, the York-based convenience store chain, has expanded its limited-time SPAM menu with over 25 items across Pennsylvania and nearby states. The post Rutter’s brings back SPAM menu with expanded lineup for limited time appeared first on Central Penn Business Journal .

articles.title: St. Luke’s unveils $252M Heart Hospital in Bethlehem
articles.summary: St. Luke’s University Health Network unveils a $252 million heart hospital on its Anderson Campus in Bethlehem, expanding cardiovascular care and patient services.

articles.title: Fulton Bank launches banking program for minority and veteran business owners
articles.summary: Lancaster-based Fulton Bank has launched a new banking program aimed at minority, women, veteran and LGBTQ business owners.

articles.title: Tyson Foods launches ride sharing program at its Lancaster County complex
articles.summary: Tyson Foods, just outside New Holland in Earl Township, has launched a ride-share program to address transportation barriers among current workers and attract prospective ones through a partnership with Enterprise, a car rental company.

articles.title: 'It's really all I wanted to do': workers at former R.R. Donnelley plants mourn closure
articles.summary: A Lancaster County man who has worked 30 years in the same printing plant under three different owners tried to fathom what would happen to him after LSC Communications closes that plant in March.

articles.title: Redevelopment of the former St. Joseph Hospital gets $1.5 million grant from the state
articles.summary: A redevelopment project of the former St. Joseph Hospital in Lancaster city was awarded $1.5 million through the state Redevelopment Assistance Capital Program, also known as RACP.

articles.title: Look inside how Amazon's central Pa. warehouses get packages to your door [photos, video]
